findings.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse() return value (Zod safeParse wrapper `{success, data}`) is stored directly as `data: { key }` in packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97, writing `{"success":true,"data":{...}}` into credential.key and permanently breaking the Google Calendar connection; needs `.data`

In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8-10, the computed key `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the literal string "[object Object]" and both computed keys collide, so minimumTokenResponseSchema strips all other fields (expiry_date, refresh_token, instance_url, scope) from the parsed result

In credential-sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-17) returns a raw fetch Response, but callers expect different shapes (HubSpot expects HubspotToken, Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM expect an axios response with .data, Google expects {data: ...}), causing TypeErrors or silent undefined reads

In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27, when the parsed response has no refresh_token the code writes the literal placeholder string "refresh_token" into the credential, destroying the stored refresh token and causing unrecoverable refresh failures

In packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:93, `credentialId` is passed where the parameter is `userId: number | null`, so the sync endpoint receives a credential id as calcomUserId and refreshes the wrong user's credential; should be `credential.userId`

In packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:76-98, an unconditional token-refresh HTTP round trip plus a prisma.credential.update runs on every Salesforce service construction with no expiry check, adding a blocking network call to every booking/availability path and risking Salesforce OAuth rate limits

In packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:87, `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw` is an unreliable success check because statusText is empty over HTTP/2 and for non-200 2xx responses; use response.ok/response.status

In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29, the webhook secret is compared with non-constant-time `!==` on an attacker-controlled header; should use crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers
In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29, a duplicated webhook secret header arrives as string[] and will never match the comparison
In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29, the header comparison silently depends on the header name being lowercase

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 has no HTTP method check, so the handler accepts GET/PUT/DELETE; a GET with the secret in headers is CSRF-adjacent and makes the endpoint cacheable/loggable; gate on req.method === "POST"

In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31, `schema.parse()` throws on a malformed body with no try/catch, returning a 500 (with a Zod stack in dev) instead of a 400; use safeParse and return 400

In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-59, `symmetricDecrypt(...)` and `JSON.parse(...)` are unguarded, so a wrong encryption key, non-encrypted payload, or non-JSON plaintext throws a 500 instead of a 400, and the `|| ""` key fallback makes a misconfigured deploy fail with an opaque crypto error

In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-16, the outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication (no webhook secret/signature) and the response status is never checked, so error pages from the sync endpoint are passed downstream and parsed as token responses

In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-88, the decrypted keys blob is written to credential.key without validating it against the app's key schema, silently installing an unusable credential that only fails later at use time
In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-88, the update path doesn't reset `credential.invalid`, so a credential previously marked invalid stays disabled after fresh keys are synced

No tests accompany the new auth-bearing surface: app-credential.ts (secret mismatch, disabled-sharing, unknown user/app, bad ciphertext) and parseRefreshTokenResponse (round-trip of expiry_date/refresh_token)

In packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:92-94, `if (!accessTokenParsed.success) return Promise.reject(...)` is dead/unreachable code because parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws on failure

In packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:76, the refresh URL is hardcoded to https://login.salesforce.com, breaking sandbox (test.salesforce.com) and My Domain orgs; the stored instance_url should be used

In packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:262, removing the console.error dropped the Zod error and raw Microsoft response, so failures surface only as the generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" with no diagnostic context

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29, the webhook secret is compared with non-constant-time `!==` on an attacker-controlled header; should use crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler checks authorization by directly comparing an attacker-controlled header value to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` using `!==` (string equality). This comparison is not constant-time and may short-circuit on the first mismatching byte/char, creating a potential timing side-channel for guessing the secret. This is a verifiable security weakness present in the added code at the header check in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29, a duplicated webhook secret header arrives as string[] and will never match the comparison

adjudication.rationale: The code compares `req.headers[<name>]` directly to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. While the TypeScript type for `req.headers[...]` allows `string | string[] | undefined`, in Node/Next API routes non-`set-cookie` headers are typically represented as a single string (multiple occurrences are generally concatenated into a comma-separated string rather than a `string[]`). The finding assumes the custom webhook header will arrive as `string[]` when duplicated, which is not a behavior shown or guaranteed by this diff, and even if multiple values did exist, rejecting the request is not clearly incorrect. Thus this is speculative rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29, the header comparison silently depends on the header name being lowercase

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the code indexes `req.headers[...]` using `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` (or the default). In Node/Next, `req.headers` keys are normalized to lowercase. If the env var is set to a non-lowercase name (e.g. `Calcom-Webhook-Secret`), `req.headers[thatValue]` will be `undefined` and the check will fail, rejecting valid requests. The code relies on the header name being lowercase and does not enforce/normalize it (e.g. via `.toLowerCase()`), so this is a real correctness/operational footgun introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 has no HTTP method check, so the handler accepts GET/PUT/DELETE; a GET with the secret in headers is CSRF-adjacent and makes the endpoint cacheable/loggable; gate on req.method === "POST"

adjudication.rationale: In the new Next.js API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does not check `req.method` at all. It proceeds to `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` regardless of method. For non-POST requests (e.g., GET/DELETE) `req.body` is typically empty/undefined, so `zod.parse` will throw and (since it’s not caught) likely results in a 500 instead of a clean 405/400. Separately, allowing GET/etc. also broadens the endpoint surface unnecessarily even though it uses a shared-secret header. Gating to POST is a reasonable, verifiable fix implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-59, `symmetricDecrypt(...)` and `JSON.parse(...)` are unguarded, so a wrong encryption key, non-encrypted payload, or non-JSON plaintext throws a 500 instead of a 400, and the `|| ""` key fallback makes a misconfigured deploy fail with an opaque crypto error

adjudication.rationale: The new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` directly does `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""))` with no try/catch or validation around either operation. If the encryption key is missing/misconfigured (the code explicitly falls back to an empty string) or if `reqBody.keys` is not decryptable / the decrypted plaintext is not valid JSON, `symmetricDecrypt(...)` and/or `JSON.parse(...)` can throw, which will bubble up as an unhandled exception and result in a 500 response rather than a controlled 4xx. This is a concrete robustness/correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-16, the outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication (no webhook secret/signature) and the response status is never checked, so error pages from the sync endpoint are passed downstream and parsed as token responses

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `refreshOAuthTokens` performs a `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` and returns the raw response without adding any authentication material (no shared secret header, signature, bearer token, etc.). Unlike the inbound webhook handler added in the diff (which validates `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`), this outbound call does not send a secret at all. Additionally, `refreshOAuthTokens` does not check `response.ok` / status codes before returning, so non-2xx responses (including HTML error pages) can be propagated to callers, which then attempt to treat the result as a token response (e.g., downstream code expects token-like data). This behavior is directly verifiable in the diff at lines 8–16 of `refreshOAuthTokens.ts`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/lib/constants.ts:103, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED = A && B` evaluates to the value of CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY (type string | undefined) rather than a boolean, so logging/serializing the flag leaks the encryption key; wrap in Boolean(...)

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding references `packages/lib/constants.ts:103` and claims a specific implementation (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED = A && B`) that would leak `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. However, the diff provided does not include any changes to `packages/lib/constants.ts` nor does it show the definition of `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`. The diff only shows usages/imports of `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`, so the alleged string-typed flag/leak cannot be verified from the diff and is therefore speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-88, the decrypted keys blob is written to credential.key without validating it against the app's key schema, silently installing an unusable credential that only fails later at use time

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, after decrypting and `JSON.parse`-ing `reqBody.keys`, the code directly persists it to `prisma.credential.update/create` as `key: keys` with no validation against any app-specific credential schema (it only checks `appStoreMetadata` for slug/type). This can store malformed/incomplete credential payloads that won’t be rejected here and may only fail later when the credential is used/parsed elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-88, the update path doesn't reset `credential.invalid`, so a credential previously marked invalid stays disabled after fresh keys are synced
